Prepare a Dataset for Survival Analysis

Source: R/processing_dataset.R
processing_dataset.Rd

Takes a data frame or reads a file, renames the columns of the treatment arm, the survival time and the event or censoring indicator to ARM, SURVTIME and EVENT, keeps the requested covariate and stratification columns, and checks the values. The treatment arm is returned as a factor whose first level is the control arm, so that every function of the package uses the same reference arm.

Usage

processing_dataset(
  dataset,
  column_arm,
  column_survtime,
  column_cnsr = NULL,
  column_event = NULL,
  column_covariates = NULL,
  column_strata = NULL,
  control_arm = NULL
)

Arguments

dataset

A data frame, or a single character string with the path of a CSV (.csv), Excel (.xlsx, .xls), SAS (.sas7bdat) or SAS transport (.xpt) file. Excel files need the package readxl and SAS files the package haven.

column_arm

Name of the column with the treatment arm.

column_survtime

Name of the column with the survival time. The times must be positive.

column_cnsr

Name of the column with the censoring indicator (1 = censored, 0 = event). The default is NULL.

column_event

Name of the column with the event indicator (1 = event, 0 = censored). The default is NULL. When both column_cnsr and column_event are given, column_event is used.

column_covariates

Character vector with the names of the columns kept as covariates for adjusted hazard ratios. The default is NULL (none).

column_strata

Character vector with the names of the columns kept as stratification factors. The default is NULL (none).

control_arm

Value of the treatment arm used as the control (reference) arm. The default is NULL, which uses the first level when the arm column is a factor and the first value in sorted order otherwise.

Value

A data frame with the columns ARM (factor with the control arm as the first level), SURVTIME (numeric), EVENT (integer, 1 = event, 0 = censored), followed by the covariate and stratification columns with their original names. Rows with a missing value in any of these columns are removed with a warning.

Examples

raw <- generate_dummy_survival_data(
  arm = c("Control", "Treatment"), n = c(50, 50),
  hazards = log(2) / c(12, 18), dropout_per_year = 0.1, seed = 1
)
dat <- processing_dataset(raw, column_arm = "ARM",
                          column_survtime = "SURVTIME",
                          column_cnsr = "CNSR", control_arm = "Control")
head(dat)
#>       ARM  SURVTIME EVENT
#> 1 Control 13.073965     1
#> 2 Control 20.457002     1
#> 3 Control  2.522524     1
#> 4 Control  2.420183     1
#> 5 Control  7.549369     1
#> 6 Control 50.118681     1
levels(dat$ARM)
#> [1] "Control"   "Treatment"
